title: Tenant warmup rebalance and fallback tuning to prevent mid-day capacity spillovers
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
During a multi-tenant production surge on 2025-02-09 we observed sustained spillover from high-throughput tenants into adjacent reserved pools. This caused mid-day capacity shortages for three enterprise customers with Reserved Pools + Burst enabled. Symptoms: elevated tail latency, allocation queuing, and throttled burst grants despite visible idle GPU headroom in sibling pools.

This ticket tracks the bug fix and mitigations: adjust warmup/rebalance heuristics, improve fallback routing to pre-warmed standby slots, and add telemetry for detecting cross-tenant spillover earlier. It also collects comms artifacts and customer post-incident follow-up tasks.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Provision two reserved pools A (high-burst tenant) and B (enterprise tenant) in same region and capacity class. 2) Configure tenant A with aggressive burst policy and warmup disabled. 3) Run an SLO-shaped traffic generator against tenant A: 70% sustained CPU/GPU token churn for 12 minutes with 5s p99 tails. 4) Observe allocator decisions: steady evictions or delayed preemption in pool A followed by spill requests targeted to pool B's headroom. 5) Notice pool B experiences allocation queuing and increased latency despite headroom metrics showing free slots in cold pools.

Note: requires running the capacity simulator (internal repo: infra/capacity-sim) to reliably reproduce locally.
root_cause:
Preliminary analysis indicates two contributing issues: 1) Warmup signal suppression: the predictive warmup component delays provisioning of standby slots when it detects very recent cold starts, due to an overly conservative cooldown window. This allowed bursts to exceed instantaneous available slots. 2) Fallback routing uses a scoring function that undervalues pre-warmed standby slots in adjacent pools because of stale KV cache metrics; allocator preferred cross-pool spill with slower setup latency, causing transient double-booking and apparent headroom mismatch.

There is also an amplification effect from the burst-credit accounting system where pending spill requests hold soft reservations that block faster pre-warm allocations until a timeout expires.
mitigation:
SHORT TERM (hotfixs):
- Patch autoscaler warmup cooldown from 5m -> 45s to allow faster standby slot creation for repeated bursts (hotfix branch: github.com/redwood/inference/PR#5312).
- Temporarily disable soft reservation hold-time for spill requests (config flag: allocator.spill_hold_ms -> 0) to allow immediate reallocation to pre-warmed slots.
- Add emergency fallback rule to prefer pre-warmed standby slots in same tenant-cluster before cross-pool spill.

LONG TERM:
- Replace single-value KV metrics with time-decayed estimators for slot warmness.
- Add proactive per-tenant warmup budget that ramps with observed burst frequency.
- Add end-to-end test in capacity-sim and e2e harness to catch regression.
postmortem_actions: Deploy warmup cooldown hotfix to canary (region-us-east-1) and monitor for 24h
Add time-decayed warmness metric and retire stale KV cache window (runtime-1.20 backlog)
Create synthetic regression test in infra/capacity-sim that simulates repeated mid-day bursts
Ship telemetry dashboard: 'spillover-index' and alert on >3 cross-pool spill events per 15m
Customer comms: send RCA draft to affected customers and schedule technical follow-up call
